abstracts.abstract: This study proposes a novel theoretical framework that reconceptualizes the relationship between IT governance mechanisms and organizational agility in the context of digital transformation. Drawing upon dynamic capabilities theory and contingency perspectives, we introduce the concept of "governance flexibility" as a multidimensional construct that fundamentally challenges traditional hierarchical governance assumptions in information systems research. Through rigorous theoretical analysis of 78 organizations across multiple industries, we demonstrate that traditional IT governance models developed for stable environments exhibit systematic inadequacies when confronted with rapid technological change and market disruption. Our framework introduces three novel constructs—adaptive governance orientation, distributed decision rights, and sensing-based IT alignment—that collectively explain how organizations achieve superior agility outcomes. The theoretical contributions are threefold: first, we challenge the prevailing assumption that formalization enhances governance effectiveness; second, we establish a new paradigm that positions governance as a dynamic capability rather than a static control mechanism; third, we provide testable propositions that open new research directions for IS management scholarship. This paradigmatic shift offers significant implications for IT governance theory and practice, suggesting that organizations must fundamentally redesign their governance architectures to thrive in increasingly volatile business environments.

Despite extensive research on technology adoption in information systems, current theoretical models inadequately address the complex dynamics of AI technology acceptance in organizational contexts. This study extends the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) by integrating organizational culture dimensions and perceived organizational support as critical antecedents, thereby addressing a significant gap in understanding enterprise AI adoption. We develop an enhanced theoretical model incorporating seven novel constructs derived from institutional theory and social exchange perspectives. Data collected from 423 professionals across 86 organizations reveal that the extended model explains 71% of variance in behavioral intention, representing a substantial improvement over base TAM variants. Our analysis identifies three key moderating factors—organizational innovativeness, prior technology experience, and implementation complexity—that significantly influence the strength of acceptance relationships. The findings demonstrate that cultural fit between AI systems and organizational values substantially strengthens perceived usefulness perceptions, while perceived organizational support enhances perceived ease of use through reduced technostress. This theoretical advancement contributes to business intelligence and analytics literature by providing a more nuanced understanding of enterprise AI adoption mechanisms, offering practitioners actionable guidance for AI implementation strategies that account for organizational contextual factors previously overlooked in technology adoption research.

This paper presents BlockChain-IS, a novel decentralized information system architecture that fundamentally reimagines enterprise data management through distributed ledger technology. Unlike conventional centralized systems, BlockChain-IS implements a consortium-based consensus mechanism specifically designed for multi-organizational business processes, enabling unprecedented levels of data integrity, auditability, and trust among collaborating entities. The architectural design introduces three innovative components: (1) Smart Contract-based workflow orchestration that automates cross-departmental processes without central intermediaries, (2) Hierarchical state channels that solve scalability challenges inherent in public blockchain networks while maintaining decentralization benefits, and (3) Privacy-preserving computation protocols enabling secure data sharing across organizational boundaries. We implemented a prototype system and evaluated its performance through extensive simulations and real-world pilot deployments involving four partner organizations in a supply chain consortium. Results demonstrate that BlockChain-IS achieves transaction throughput exceeding 3,000 transactions per second with sub-second finality, while providing immutable audit trails required for regulatory compliance. The system successfully addresses critical enterprise systems challenges including data provenance, automated compliance verification, and trust establishment in zero-knowledge environments. This paradigmatic contribution establishes a new design pattern for information systems development that eliminates traditional single points of failure and transforms inter-organizational data management from trust-dependent to cryptographically-verified paradigms.

This paper presents an enhanced intrusion detection framework that significantly advances the state-of-the-art in IS security monitoring for enterprise networks. Building upon traditional signature-based detection systems, we introduce a hybrid architecture combining deep learning-based anomaly detection with context-aware rule refinement mechanisms. The proposed system, EnterpriseSec-IDS, incorporates three major architectural improvements: (1) a hierarchical attention network that captures both local traffic patterns and global network behavior simultaneously, (2) an automated rule generation module that continuously updates detection signatures based on confirmed incident analysis, and (3) an explainable prediction interface that provides security analysts with interpretable threat explanations rather than opaque classification outputs. Evaluation conducted on three enterprise network datasets totaling 15 million network flows demonstrates substantial improvements: detection accuracy increases from 89.2% to 97.4%, false positive rates decrease by 62%, and mean time to detect advanced persistent threats reduces from 4.2 hours to 23 minutes. The system successfully identified 847 previously unknown attack patterns that evaded conventional detection mechanisms during a six-month production deployment. Furthermore, the explainability module received positive user feedback from security operations teams, with analysts reporting 47% reduction in time required for threat assessment and triage. This work contributes to IS security practice by delivering a deployable solution that meaningfully advances threat detection capabilities while addressing the critical need for interpretable security analytics in human-computer interaction contexts.
